ideas.truth: A new colour makes something you already own feel new again, without asking you to change anything about your life.
ideas.moment: The instant you notice your everyday backpack in a hue you've never seen it in — daylight, alone, no distractions.
ideas.key_frame: The Transit Backpack 30L in Crypto Sunray, centred on a sunlit concrete step, one pure-colour object in a quiet, muted scene.

ideas.truth: We register a bold new colour the way we register sunrise — as a signal that something has changed before we can explain why.
ideas.moment: First warm light of the morning hitting the bag on a windowsill, the colour catching before anything else does.
ideas.key_frame: Low, warm side-light raking across the bag against a charcoal backdrop, the Crypto Sunray hue glowing like an ember.

ideas.truth: A colour this loud makes you the one people notice without you having to say anything.
ideas.moment: Someone walks away down a plain grey corridor; the backpack is the only thing in the frame with any colour in it.
ideas.key_frame: Back three-quarter shot, person mid-stride down a minimal hallway, the Crypto Sunray bag the single saturated note.

why: This is a straight product/colour-drop ad, not a story about a person — Hopkins's note applies directly: colour pays when it puts the product on exhibition, so the bag alone, lit and centred, does the whole job.
treatment: We open on the exact Transit Backpack 30L from the reference photos, now in Crypto Sunray, placed dead centre on a sunlit slab of pale concrete — the kind of clean urban surface it lives on every day. Hard, warm sunlight rakes across it from one side, throwing a crisp contact shadow beneath so it reads as grounded, not floating. The background is a wide, muted warm-grey wall, kept almost bare, leaving calm space above the bag for a short headline and a calm strip below for a small site line. Nothing else sits in frame — no props, no crowd, no history, just the bag as the one saturated, pure-colour thing in an otherwise quiet, desaturated composition. It is a single still image, not a film: one shock, shown once, held.

scenes.prompt: Instagram product ad photo of the Transit Backpack 30L in Crypto Sunray, standing upright on a sunlit pale concrete step. Warm side light rakes in, casting a soft contact shadow beneath the bag. Background: a muted warm-grey wall, softly out of focus. Leave calm negative space above for a headline and a narrow strip below for a site name. The bag is the single saturated colour in a quiet, desaturated scene. Vertical 4:5, editorial commercial style.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: This is the only frame: the Transit Backpack 30L in Crypto Sunray, centred on a sunlit concrete step, warm side light casting a soft shadow beneath it, muted warm-grey wall behind, calm negative space above and below for text. The bag is the single saturated colour in an otherwise quiet, desaturated scene — the finished idea, complete and static, not building toward anything further.

finish.copy_placement: "New: Crypto Sunray" set in the calm upper-third space above the bag, in the brand's own typeface for legibility, checked against the wall's least-contrasting patch (add a thin outline if the wall tone drifts warm/light there). "mokobara.com" set small, bottom edge, same treatment, quieter weight — it's the ask, not the headline.
finish.end_card: No separate end card — this is a single static frame; the product itself, centred and fully lit, is the final (and only) image, per the customer's own request.
finish.music: Not applicable — static image, no film.

decisions.D1_idea: The moment a backpack you already know suddenly looks new to you again, simply because of its colour.
decisions.D2_conflict: The everyday carry fades into routine and stops feeling like a choice; only a genuinely new colour can interrupt that without asking the owner to change anything else about how they live.
decisions.D3_roles: Hero: the person's ordinary daily-carry life, implied but unseen. Brand: Mokobara plays the enabler, quietly refreshing a familiar object with one bold new colourway — no lecture, no persuasion, just the news.
decisions.D4_opening: First 2 seconds: a bold, still, near-centred shot of the Crypto Sunray backpack alone on sunlit concrete, in full colour and full focus, with nothing else competing for attention.
decisions.D5_brand: Product is on screen from the first (and only) second, filling most of the frame. Brand recurs solely through the on-screen text 'mokobara.com' at the bottom — one static asset, one product shot, the URL itself doing the attribution work.
decisions.D6_ask_and_end: Ask: visit mokobara.com to see the new colour, carried entirely by the small text line (no voice, since this is a still). Final frame is the product itself, centred, exactly as the customer specified — ends on product by default.

D7_product_truth.fact: The Transit Backpack 30L now comes in a colourway called Crypto Sunray.
Shape, hardware, proportions and finish match the two reference photos exactly — nothing added or altered.
The product is sold at mokobara.com.

decisions.D8_deviations: Treated this as a single static frame rather than a multi-scene film: the brief's own classification (S1_product_ad, 4:5, duration_s 0) calls for a still, so no motion, sound, or sequence is proposed — one honest image doing the whole job, in line with Ogilvy's note that a poster should carry one visual shock, not several.
decisions.D9_target_buyer: Primary buyer: an urban professional (25–40) in India who already owns or has considered a Transit Backpack 30L, follows Mokobara on Instagram, and reads a bold colour drop as a low-risk way to refresh their everyday carry without buying a whole new bag.
decisions.D10_differentiation_note: This piece uses a single static, colour-led product shot (one visual shock, no narrative) rather than a multi-scene or lifestyle sequence. We have no record of prior Mokobara creative in this session — flagging for the brand team to confirm this exact setup (concrete slab, warm rake-light, bare warm-grey wall) hasn't been used in a previous colour-drop ad before publishing.
